leads.name: Zwarte populier Noorderplantsoen Groningen
leads.species: Black Poplar (Populus nigra), possibly common poplar per register's own doubt
leads.reason: Register (netherlands-lrmb nr 1680853) calls this the tallest/thickest tree in Noorderplantsoen ('de koning van het plantsoen') but its own 2020 note records large sections of dying bark and says the tree is entering its final phase, though still alive with enough sap flow for lush foliage as of the register's last update. It also sits only 31.2 m from the already-published gro_004 (The Duck's Foot Tree of Noorderplantsoen, Ginkgo biloba) per the brief's near_published flag, a different species but close enough that a health recheck and a clearer sense of it as its own distinct stop (not just 'more park trees near the ginkgo') should happen before it ships. Not blocked: nothing here says it is dead, and a declining-but-alive veteran is exactly the kind of tree this project wants once its status is current.

leads.name: Gewone plataan RUG / Hollandse iep (pair, adjacent coordinates)
leads.species: London Plane (Platanus x acerifolia) and Dutch Elm
leads.reason: Both stand 'ingebouwd op het terrein van RUG' (built into the university's grounds); the plane's own 2023 register note says construction activity on site made it hard to inspect. Public accessibility of this specific spot on Rijksuniversiteit Groningen's terrain was not established this pass. Needs a check on whether this is open campus ground or gated, per the school/campus access test, before verifying further.

leads.name: Leilindes Pepergasthuis Groningen
leads.reason: New candidate found this pass. Register (nr 1680046) records 11 pollarded lindens ('leivorm') on the binnenplaats of the Pepergasthuis (Sint Geertruidsgasthuis), a historic hofje founded 1405 on Peperstraat, gemeente-owned, visitable listed as 'ja', in good condition with visible old tree-surgery scars from the 1980s. A genuinely good candidate (compact, historic, named ensemble) but access is a real judgement call, not a clean yes: a general source on Groningen's hofjes says 'most hofjes are freely accessible, respect residents' privacy', but this specific courtyard was recently sold to a private investor, which local reporting says has created uncertainty about its future ('mensen weten niet wat er gaat gebeuren met de binnenplaats'), and no source found this pass explicitly confirms public entry to THIS courtyard today. Per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's 'when in doubt, leave it out', left as a lead rather than shipped; a future pass should look for explicit signage/visiting-hours confirmation or treat a site visit report as decisive.

blocked.name: Beuk binnentuin Turfsingel Groningen
blocked.reason: Register's own text: stands in the 'binnentuin van een appartement' (inner courtyard of an apartment building), 'niet zichtbaar vanaf de Turfsingel' (not visible from the street), only the top of the crown visible from Hofstraat or partly from beside the Adventkerk. Private residential courtyard, not genuinely open to visitors. Blocked per the private-land rule.

blocked.name: Zwarte walnoot binnentuin Turfsingel Groningen
blocked.reason: Register's own text: stands in the 'achtertuin van een woning' (back garden of a private house). Private residential garden, not genuinely open to visitors. Blocked per the private-land rule.

blocked.name: Kaukasische vleugelnoot
blocked.reason: Register's entire history note reads: 'Boom is op 3 meter afgezaagd i.v.m. gevaarzetting' (the tree was sawn down to 3 m because it was a hazard). Not a standing, collectible tree in its recorded form; blocked as effectively removed. Could be revisited if it has since resprouted into a real crown, but nothing in the source confirms that.

blocked.name: Ruwe iep (afgezaagd)
blocked.reason: Register history: 2002 advice to thin the crown, then a 2015 observation that the tree had been sawn down to 3 m height ('afgezaagd tot op 3 meter hoogte'). Not a standing collectible tree; blocked as effectively removed, matching the brief's own flag on this entry.

blocked.name: Witte paardenkastanje Pelstergasthuis Groningen
blocked.reason: Register's own history ends: 'En toen viel de boom spontaan om! Zie laatste waarneming' (and then the tree spontaneously fell over! see latest observation), following a multi-year record of a bracket-fungus infection (dikrand tondelzwam, korstjeshoutskoolzwam) at the trunk base. Dead/fallen, confirmed by the register's own last entry. Blocked, we doen niet aan dode bomen. Also note: even before falling, it stood 'in het hofje... tegen de gevel geklemd' (clamped against the facade in the hofje courtyard), so it would also have needed an access check.

blocked.name: Zwarte moerbei RUG (Huis met de 13 tempels)
blocked.reason: Great story (planted 1780 by resident Isabella Berchuis-de Sevornin as a memento of her Zeeland youth; a 2012 plaque added by a descendant; a cutting now grows in Middelburg) but register itself lists visitable as 'op afspraak' (by appointment only) and visible as 'nee' (not visible), standing in the achtertuin (back garden) of the private house at Oude Boteringestraat 23. Blocked per the private-land rule: not genuinely open to visitors.
